content.text:
Write a short Python program that builds the eiffel tower as a detailed 3D model made of solid parts, as close to the real thing as you can: true proportions and its real structure. Model what is inside as well as the outside, as separate parts, because a person will slice it open with their hands and move through it: a ship has its hull and decks and, inside them, an engine room with engines, a shaft to the propeller, cabins and holds; a car its body and, inside, engine, seats and gearbox. If a thing has no inside (a bicycle, a lattice tower), give it every part it is known for instead.
These functions are already there. Points are (x, y, z) tuples, z up, x along its length, in any units: it gets centred and scaled afterwards. Angles are in radians.
- part(name, color): what follows belongs to this part until the next part(). The name is a plain word a person would say ("engine", "hull", "front wheel"). The color is a bright "#rrggbb": a projector shows dark colors as nothing.
- box(center, size, yaw=0): size is (dx, dy, dz). beam(a, b, w, h=None): a square bar from a to b.
- cylinder(a, b, r, r2=None, n=24): from a to b, a cone if r2 differs. sphere(center, r, n=16, size=None): size (rx, ry, rz) makes an ellipsoid. torus(center, r, tube, axis=(0, 0, 1), n=32): a ring around axis. tube(points, r, n=8): a pipe along a path.
- revolve(profile, center=(0, 0, 0), axis=(0, 0, 1), n=32): a lathe; profile is a list of (radius, height).
- loft(rings): a skin through closed rings of equal length, each a list of points: for hulls, fuselages, bodies.
- extrude(polygon, z0, z1): an outline of (x, y) points raised from z0 to z1. tri(a, b, c), quad(a, b, c, d) for anything else.
- line(points): thin lines, for cables, spokes, lattice bracing: far cheaper than solids when there are thousands.
Rules. Plain Python only, with `math` already there: no imports, no classes, no files. Use functions, loops and symmetry to get the detail cheaply: build one leg and repeat it, mirror one side to the other, loop over frames, spokes and lattice bars. 6 to 25 parts. At most 200 lines of code. No text.
Reply with JSON: "name" (what it is, 1 to 3 words) and "code" (the program).
